sentences.text: 2. Brief facts of the case are that, on 04.08.2014 at about 7.30 pm., the deceased was crossing Tumkur- Bangalore NH-4 main road, on Kengal Kempohali Bus Stand, at that time, a KSRTC bus bearing Reg. No.KA-19-F-3098 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased.
As a result of which, the deceased fell down and wheel of the bus run on the head of the deceased and the deceased died on the spot.

3. Heard the arguments from both sides and perused the records.
4.

Smt.Aruna Bhat, learned counsel appearing for Sri G.Lakshmeesh submitted that, in the present case, the accident was caused on the national highway while the deceased was crossing the national highway near Kengal Kempohalli Bus Stand, Tumkur-Bangalore NH-4.
Therefore, submitted that the national highway is mainly meant for plying the vehicle with speed and crossing of the national highway is prohibited other than the fixed place for crossing the road.

Therefore, submitted that upon perusing Ex.P.3-Panchanama and Ex.P.4-spot sketch, the accident was caused near the divider, which means, it is the deceased has taken the risk while crossing the road, even though,
observing the bus that was coming on the national highway.
Therefore, submitted that the deceased has also contributed 50% of his negligence and caused the accident.
Further submitted that the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side, therefore, prays for reducing the same.

5. On the other hand, Sri P.Shivakumar, learned counsel for the claimants submitted that in the complaint the entire allegation is made against the driver of the bus and resultantly, the charge sheet is filed against the driver of the bus.
Therefore, submitted that the entire rash and negligent aspect is on the driver of the KSRTC bus and caused the accident.
Therefore, submitted that the Tribunal is correct in holding that the driver of the bus was completely rash and negligent in driving the bus.
Therefore, prays for dismissal of the appeal.
Further submitted that the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lesser side.
Therefore, prays for enhancement of compensation.
6. Undisputedly, the accident was caused near Kengal Kempohalli Bus Stand, Tumkur-Bangalore NH-4.

Though, the charge sheet is filed against the driver of the KSRTC bus, but the rash and negligent aspect is to be considered in the claim proceedings and the evidence placed before it,
without being influenced by the charge sheet upon the principle of res ipsa loquitur (the thing speaks for itself).
The bus was coming from Tumkur to Bangalore side.
The road is NH.4.
The place of accident is shown near the divider towards southern side.

The national highway is primarily meant for plying of the vehicle with speed and crossing of national highway from one edge to The Managing Director vs Sri. Ramji @ Ramuji @ Ramjilal on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81428246/

sentences.text: another edge is prohibited other than the fixed area meant for crossing the road like sky walk, sky bridge etc.
Therefore, crossing the national highway upon seeing the vehicle plying on the national highway is nothing but inviting the risk while crossing the national highway.

Upon considering the spot mahazar -Ex.P.3 and spot sketch-Ex.P4 respectively, the KSRTC bus was moving from the correct side of the road from Tumkur to Bangalore, but the spot sketch and spot mahazar reveals that either the deceased was crossing from southern to northern direction and had crossed the divider or while attempting to cross the road from northern to southern direction, then the claimant was about to cross the divider, at that juncture, the accident was caused.
Therefore, the entire negligence cannot be attributed on the part of the driver of KSRTC bus.
The evidence of R.W.1 who is the driver of the KSRTC bus is also to be appreciated that he was driving the bus with moderate speed and the deceased had come suddenly.

Therefore, he could not apply brake and even though,
he could apply brakes, but the deceased himself came in contact with the bus.

Therefore, upon visualizing the entire evidence on record with regard to manner of accident, as discussed above, it is found that the deceased had also contributed his negligence towards the accident.
When the deceased was crossing the road and the bus is coming, then it cannot be said that the deceased has not seen the bus coming on the national highway.
Therefore, even the deceased by knowing the fact that the bus was coming and also road is the national highway, it means the deceased has taken the risk while crossing the road.
Therefore, the deceased has also contributed his negligence.

7. Even though, the learned counsel for the appellant- KSRTC has argued that the deceased had contributed 50% of rash and negligent, but considering the proportionate degree of rash and negligent, even though, the driver could have seen the deceased crossing the road, the driver could have applied brake immediately by slowing down the bus, then the accident could have been avoided.
Therefore, the ratio of rash and negligent - 10 - aspect is to be apportioned as 25% on the deceased and 75% on the driver of the KSRTC bus.
Therefore, the finding made by the Tribunal in this regard is hereby modified as above stated.
Regarding quantum of compensation:

8. In the present case, the Tribunal has awarded compensation as follow:
1 Towards loss of Rs. 8,87,250/- dependency 2 Towards loss of Rs. 40,000/- love and affection 3 Towards funeral Rs. 25,000/-
expenses Total Rs. 9,52,250/-
9.
The deceased is a bachelor aged 24 years as on the date of the accident.
The Tribunal has taken the income at Rs.7,000/- pm., which is on the lesser side.

Considering the year of accident as 2014,
the notional income has to be taken at Rs.8,500/- per month as per - 11 - The Managing Director vs Sri. Ramji @ Ramuji @ Ramjilal on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81428246/

The Tribunal has committed error in choosing the multiplier according to the age of the younger parent of the deceased.
But the appropriate multiplier is to be taken into consideration as per the age of the deceased.
Therefore, the appropriate multiplier applicable is 18.

As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi1 as the deceased was aged 24 years as on the date of the accident, 40% of income is to be added towards loss of future prospects in life.

sentences.text: Since, the deceased was a bachelor, 50% of income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses.
Therefore, the loss of dependency is re-
calculated and quantified as follows:

Rs.8,500/- + Rs.3,400/- (40% of Rs.8,500/-)=Rs.11,900/- Rs.11,900/- x 50% x 18 x 12=Rs.12,85,200/- (2017) 16 SCC 680 - 12 - Accordingly, compensation of Rs.12,85,200/- is awarded under the head loss of dependency.
10. The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of love and affection.
The loss of love and affection and loss of consortium are having the same connotation.
As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Limited Vs. Nanu Ram & Others2, each claimants are entitled for Rs.40,000/-.

sentences.text: Hence, in the present case, there are four dependants.

Therefore, compensation of Rs.1,76,000/- (Rs.40,000/- x 4 dependants =
Rs.1,60,000/- + 10% escalation) with 10% escalation is awarded under the head loss of consortium including loss of love and affection.
The compensation of Rs.30,000/- is awarded under the heads transportation, obsequies ceremony, funeral expenses and loss of estate.

sentences.text: The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.9,52,250/-.

Since the deceased has also contributed his negligence to the extent of 25%, the appellants/claimants are entitled to only 75%
out of the total compensation amount of Rs.14,91,200/-.

Hence, the appellants/claimants are entitled to compensation of - 14 - Rs.11,18,400/- (Rs.14,91,200/- x 75%) with the rate of interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.

14. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i. MFA.No.5466/2015 filed by the KSRTC is allowed-in-part.
ii. MFA.No.5617/2015 filed by the claimants is allowed-in-part.
iii.

The impugned judgment and award dated 29.04.2015 in MVC.No.4280/2014 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore (SCCH-17), is hereby modified to the extent that the appellants/claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.11,18,400/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
No order as to costs.
v. Registry is directed to transmit the TCR along with copy of this order to the Tribunal forthwith.
vi. The amount in deposit made by the KSRTC shall be transmitted to the Tribunal forthwith.
vii. Draw award accordingly.
